programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Nuair tha Boban is Fuigheag a’ campadh sa ghàrradh-chùil, tha rudeigin bhon taobh a-muigh a’ cruthachadh faileas air an teant’ ‘s tha Fuigheag draghail mun seo. Ach dè th’ ann? When Boban and Fuigheag go camping in the back garden, there’s something from outside creating a shadow on the tent. Fuigheag is worried, what is it though?

programme.title: Dòtaman
programme.desc: Prògram Dòtaman as an tasglann bho 1989 air a' chuspair sròinean ann an cuideachd spòrsail Dhonnie is Rhoda. Tha ceòl, òran, sgeulachd is cleasachd gu leòr ri fhaotainn. Feuch gun coimhead sibh airson na caraidean Cagnaidh is Crotal, agus gum bi sibh deiseal airson Nelson is Napoleon aig a' ghleoc! A treat from the Dotaman archives. Recorded in 1989, this edition explores the topic of noses in the fun, creative and colourful company of Donnie and Rhoda. Look out for furry friends Cagnaidh and Crotal and be prepared to count along with Nelson and Napoleon at the Dotaman clock!

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air a caraidean Meaban is Moo sa bhothan aca gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha i ag iarraidh orra trì rudan ann an cumadh ceart-cheàrnaich a lorg. Tha treallaich gu leòr sa bhothan agus feumaidh Meaban is Moo a dhol a rùraich gus an lorg. Linda visits her friends Meaban and Moo at their hut to set them challenges. In this programme, she tasks them with finding three rectangular shaped items. Their hut is full of junk so Meaban and Moo need to have a good rummage in order to find them!

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha camara aig Àtaidh. Tha aig a h-uile duine ri rudeigin spòrsail a dhèanamh. Chan fhada gus a bheil Nìp a’ faighinn cothrom cuideachd agus tha na dealbhan aigeasan uabhasach sònraichte. Abney's got a camera and everybody does something fun with it! Soon, Neep gets a go too, and his photos are very special.

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Grandad's gnomes go missing and Stan's mystery deepens when he finds a tiny human handprint! The gnomes can't really have come to life, can they?! Tha frìdean an t-Seanair a' dol a dhìth,'s tha rùn-dìomhair Dan a' dol am meud nuair a lorgas e làrach-làimhe beag bìodach bho dhaonna. 'N eil rian gun tàinig na fridean beò, a bheil?!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Ellen NicDhòmhnaill a’ leughadh Harriet an Nighean as Làidire san t-Saoghal. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Ben Lerwill, a dhealbhachadh le Beatrice Blue agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. Ellen MacDonald reads Harriet an Nighean as Làidire san t-Saoghal by Ben Lerwill, illustrated by Beatrice Blue and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha e tighinn am follais gur e ionnsramaid-chiùil a th’ ann am bodhaig Phòil agus thathar ag iarraidh air àite fear de bhuill a’ chòmhlain as fheàrr leis, Na Coin Chaola, a ghabhail. Dave discovers that his body is a musical instrument and is asked to replace a band member in his favourite group, The Whippets.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Thathar a’ dèanamh deiseil airson cuirm-chluich bhliadhnail a’ bhaile, is tha Anna ag iarraidh pàirt na bana-phrionnsa. Ach ’s ann a tha pàirtean nam bana-bhuidseach air a thoirt dhi fhèin, Pòl agus Granaidh, is tha iad a’ feuchainn ri shealltainn gun urrainn crìoch shona a bhith aig sgeulachd nam bana-bhuidseach cuideachd. Grimsby is putting on its annual community play and Anna wants the role of princess. Cast as a witch instead, the Spuds set out to prove that witches can have happy endings, too.

programme.title: Stri
programme.desc: Tha preasantairean CBBC ALBA uabhasach fhèin measail air dùbhlain ach saoil cò shoirbhicheas is Mhairi a’ tadhal orra? The CBBC ALBA presenters love a good challenge but who will emerge victorious as Mhairi joins them?

programme.title: Mystique no 375
programme.desc: Fiolm goirid airson òigridh. Sgeulachd nighean òg aig am bheil miann a bhith air àrd-ùrlar. Short drama for the younger audience, set in Largs, on the south west coast of Scotland. Ten-year-old Kriselle lives with her dad, who manages a rundown seaside theatre. After school and during the holidays, Kriselle helps her dad, Mackie, with the running of it, along with her cheeky best pal, Roland. Kriselle is wise beyond her years, and has a hankering for being on stage herself - but something is holding her back: the theatre is fast losing money, and Mackie worries that it may have to close down. Then, Kriselle has a brainwave: wouldn't the audience love to see a show with Frangipane, the biggest star around? When the glamorous and exotic Frangipane turns up, things don't go as smoothly as Kriselle hoped. And as the big performance night looms, it's chaos - can Kriselle save the day, and, with Roland, save the theatre? And do she and Frangipane have more in common than they could ever have imagined?

programme.title: A’ Chùil
programme.desc: Tha Choirstaidh air ais le prògram eile bhon stiùidio aice A’ Chùil. Sa phrògram seo bheir i sùil air an neach-ealain ainmeil Hilma Af Klint agus seallaidh i dhut mar a nì thu dealbh anns an stoidhle aicese. Choirstaidh is back with another programme from her studio A’ Chùil. She takes a look at the famous artist Hilma Af Klint, and shows you how to make your own picture in her style.

programme.title: Saor no Daor
programme.desc: Best friends Christy and Zach plan the ultimate day out for each other in Inverness. Christy has £150 to spend, while Zach has just £40. The pair try a local delicacy and head out on Loch Ness to find Nessie. Tha fìor dheagh charaidean Christy agus Zach a’ cur air dòigh latha air leth dha chèile ann an Inbhir Nis. Tha 150 not aig Christy san sporran s gun ach 40 aig Zach. Tha iad a’ blasadh air sàr bhiadh ionadail agus a’ lorg Nessie ann an Loch Nis. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: Abair gu bheil treat air leth aig Abigail – Tost Frangach. An dearbh bhiadh airson brunch le càirdean is caraidean. Abigail has a special treat in store in the form of a tasty french toast snack. It's perfect for that table brunch spread when friends and family visit. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: We meet learner Andrew Gourlay from Fife, and Calum Maclean is in Perthshire to explore the myths connected to one of Britain’s oldest trees.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Garradh Phadruig
programme.desc: Summer has arrived and Peter finally gets to work on his front garden. Tha’n samhradh air tighinn is tha Pàdruig a’sealltainn ri gàrradh aghaidh an taighe.

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc: Anns an treas phrògram, tha Kate a’ tadhal air Rubha an Dùnain ann an cuideachd Choinnich MhicIlleathain is ag ionnsachadh beagan mu eachdraidh nan Lochlannach, tha i cuideachd a’ coinneachadh ris a’ phìobaire, Decker Forrest, a tha ag innse dhi mu phìobairean ainmeil MhicCruimein. Tha i a’ faighinn cothrom snàmh agus còcaireachd a dhèanamh còmhla ri Clare Coghill, tè a tha a’ cosnadh cliù mar shàr chòcaire. Agus bidh i cuideachd a’ tadhal air àiteachan a tha gu math ainmeil san Eilean Sgitheanach, nam measg, taigh-solais Rubha na h-Eist, Bàgh Thalasgair agus na h-Eileanan Ascrib. Kate visits Rubha an Dùnain in the company of Coinneach Maclean, where she learns a little about Viking history. She also meets piper Decker Forrest, who tells her about the famous MacCrimmon pipers. Kate gets an opportunity to swim and cook with Clare Coghill, who is making a name for herself as an expert chef. She also visits famous Skye landmarks Neist Point, Talisker Bay and the Ascrib Islands. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rudan Beaga Bòidheach/Life’s Little Things
programme.desc: Tha Niamh NicFhionghain a’ coinneachadh daoine òga eile gus rudan beaga fheuchainn a tha a’ toirt toileachas dhaibh. Bho Iòga air mullach cnoc, a bhith a’ sgrìobhadh bàrdachd, gu furachas, dòigh-beatha a’ bhana-campachaidh no a bhith a’ cluich camanachd – tha tòrr ann air an urrainn dhut a bhith taingeil an uair a tha thu air a’ bhlàr a-muigh. Skye digital creator Niamh Mackinnon meets other young people to try out the different little activities that spark joy for them. From hilltop yoga, or writing poems, to mindfulness, camper van life or playing shinty - there’s so much to appreciate when you just get out there. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: Tha Cathy Nicdhòmhnaill a’ bruidhinn ri clann a’ mhansa. Cathy Macdonald talks to children of the manse.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap based on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Fàilte gu Fraochy Bay , baile nach fhaic thu a h-uile là! Is iomadh annas a tha ri fhaicinn sa bhaile , agus sin gun ghuth air càil ach muinntir a bhaile fhèin. Tha an stèisean rèidio agus telebhisean airson dearbhadh am bheil dreach uaine air a bhaile. Welcome to the colourful and unusual world of Fraochy Bay, a miniature metropolis somewhere off the fringes of the map. Fraochy Bay FM and WebTV search for some environmental friends.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram spioradail le laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean à Coats ann am Pàislig, air a lìbhrigeadh le Iain MacFhionghain. Am measg na seinneadairean bidh Raonaid Nic an Fhùcadair, Iain ‘Costello’ MacÌomhair, Rona NicLeòid ‘s Donnchadh MacLeòid, agus an còisir Soisgeul fo stiùir Gareth Fuller. Bidh Moira NicÌomhair a’ meòrachadh air cuspair creideimh le leughadh agus smuain. Cuideachd, dàn is seallaidhean spioradail à Tiriodh ann an companachd Dòmhnall Eachann Meek, agus bidh Chloe Steele a’ toirt dhuinn seirm adhraidh air a’ phìob à Manachainn nan Lios. Iain MacKinnon presents with a mix of hymns, psalms and readings from Coats in Paisley. Amongst the singers performing are Rachel Walker, Iain ‘Costello’ Maciver, Rona MacLeod & Duncan MacLeod and the choir Soisgeul, conducted by Gareth Fuller. Moira MacIver reflects on beliefs with selected reading and thought, spiritual poetry and landscapes from Tiree in the company of Donald E Meek, and Chloe Steele performs a tune of worship on the pipes from Beauly Priory. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke unpicks the reasons behind the dazzling revolution that gave birth to classical Greek art, asking how the Greeks got so good so quickly. He travels to the beautiful Valley of the Temples in Agrigento, and to the island of Mozia to see the astonishing charioteer found there in 1979, and marvels at the athletic bodies of the warriors dragged from the seabed - the Riace Bronzes. It was a creative explosion that covered architecture, sculpting in marble, casting in bronze, even painting on vases. Perhaps the most powerful factor was also its greatest legacy - a fascination with the naked human body.

programme.title: Stolen: Catching the Art Thieves
programme.desc: In 1994, Munch’s The Scream is ripped from a gallery wall in Oslo. The detectives leading the investigation describe a complex and dangerous investigation which exposes the lengths to which criminals will go to gain a get-out-of-jail card for murder.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: At the home of Scottish football, Glasgow’s Hampden Park stadium, Michael admires the oldest football trophy in the world and hears how the 'passing game' was born there. From Scotland’s busiest railway station, the splendid Glasgow Central, Michael heads to the M8 motorway to see 16 lanes of traffic slicing through the city centre. At the Kelvingrove Art Gallery, Michael hears how, after the Second World War, artist Joan Eardley set up a studio amid the tenements of Townhead and painted children from Glasgow’s slums. Michael finishes this leg of the journey in the planned, modernist new town of Cumbernauld, where he hears about the utopian ideals that shaped its design and architecture.

programme.title: Walking With...
programme.desc: Broadcaster Kate Garraway goes for an invigorating walk along the edge of the Cotswold Hills. As she passes through the patch where Kate first cut her teeth as a reporter, she takes time to appreciate the stunning landscapes. From the panoramic viewpoint of Painswick Beacon, Kate descends through beech woods to the village of Upton St Leonards, soaking up the sounds of nature as she goes. From there she climbs Cooper’s Hill and wanders down to the church at Great Witcombe. Kate relishes the chance to have nothing to do but take in the 'joy and rhythm of the countryside' as she crosses the gentle, rolling hills with just a 360-degree camera for company. Along the way, she meets local craftspeople who are inspired by the ‘living theatre’ of the landscapes. Kate finds her natural surroundings a source of inspiration and resilience as she reflects on a year of challenges and change.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth realises that Richard is bored after taking early retirement and provides him with a hobby - being artistic with a video camera. However, it's a decision she will live to regret.

programme.title: One Foot in the Grave
programme.desc: Victor and Margaret head off for a weekend at the seaside. Victor is presented with a most unusual and unwelcome gift.

programme.title: She-Wolves: England's Early Queens
programme.desc: In the medieval and Tudor world there was no question in people's minds about the order of God's creation - men ruled and women didn't. A king was a warrior who literally fought to win power then battled to keep it. Yet despite everything that stood in their way, a handful of extraordinary women did attempt to rule medieval and Tudor England. In this series, historian Dr Helen Castor explores seven queens who challenged male power, the fierce reactions they provoked and whether the term 'she wolves' was deserved. Eight hundred years ago, Matilda came within a hair's breadth of being the first woman to be crowned queen of England in her own right. Castor explores how Matilda reached this point and why her bid for the throne ultimately failed. Her daughter-in-law Eleanor of Aquitaine was an equally formidable woman. Despite being remembered as the queen of courtly love, in reality during her long life she divorced one king and married another, only to lead a rebellion against him. She only finally achieved the power she craved in her seventies.

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Sam Willis looks at the history of the castle from its first appearance with the Normans in 1066 to the longest siege on English soil at Kenilworth Castle 200 years later. The castle arrived as an instrument of invasion but soon became a weapon with which unruly barons challenged the Crown. Tintagel Castle, the place where King Arthur is said to have been conceived, is also on the itinerary. It remains one of the most evocative of castles to this day, drawing visitors from around the world with its tales of myth and legend.

programme.title: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
programme.desc: Why did the entire world stand by in 1994 as nearly one million people were murdered over one hundred days of incomprehensible terror in Rwanda? American diplomats describe events on the ground and in Washington as this tragedy unfolded. What did the White House know, when did they know it and why didn’t they act? The horrendous results of ignoring the genocide in Rwanda haunts the Washington decision-makers to this day. President Clinton refers to it as 'the greatest failure of my life'.

programme.title: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
programme.desc: Three years after the civil war in Bosnia, the world looked like a very different place. The Bosnian genocide had been stopped, but Muslim separatists in the Kosovo region rekindled old conflicts that led President Clinton’s White House to consider Serbian President Milošević’s regime a threat to their own civilians. With post-Soviet Russia in crisis, Boris Yeltsin, the Russian president, criticised at home for being 'an American puppet', strongly opposed any western intervention against their old allies in the Balkans. Nato did intervene, but at what cost? Boris Yeltsin is forced to resign, leaving a young and promising KGB officer named Vladimir Putin to take his place.

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke unpicks the reasons behind the dazzling revolution that gave birth to classical Greek art, asking how the Greeks got so good so quickly. It was a creative explosion that covered architecture, sculpting in marble, casting in bronze, even painting on vases. Perhaps the most powerful factor was also its greatest legacy - a fascination with the naked human body.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's a milestone moment for the park's young Amur tigers as sisters Ginger Biscuit and Seeka begin preparations to leave home. As part of the international breeding programme, they'll soon move to new collections to help secure the future of one of the world's rarest big cats. But before they can go, the keepers face the challenge of preparing them for life apart and training them to enter their transport crates for the very first time. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at an extraordinary conservation adventure when Longleat keepers travelled to Tanzania to help renowned conservationist Tony Fitzjohn relocate endangered African wild dogs. This remarkable story would go on to influence conservation work back at the park for years to come. Elsewhere, Megan introduces the park's emus to an unusual new treat, while the recently arrived maned wolves begin settling into their new home as keepers learn to tell the three sisters apart.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: Two men are lured to a spot in Cambridgeshire under the pretence of a business meeting. But they’re kidnapped, threatened with weapons by masked men and forced to transfer a large amount of the company’s money. Police need to unpick a complicated web of phone calls and CCTV to find their moment of proof. And a couple who become ill after eating curry are found to have been poisoned. With one person dead, police are hunting for a murderer.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A fibre analyst uses a groundbreaking technique to solve the murder of 91-year-old Edwin Hiles, and a forensic fire investigator helps to uncover the truth behind a tragic house fire.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: An uncle is on hand to help his niece create a family home in Bristol. Dion’s in the dark in Leeds, but it’s nothing a lick of white paint won’t sort out. Jacqui’s in west London, where she’s hoping to get a free massage from the new owner of a ground floor flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Knock knock! Who’s there? It’s Danny Sebastian banging on about the history of door knockers, from Ancient Greece right through to the lion on the famous front door of 10 Downing Street. In Caroline Hawley’s saleroom, Danny sees an impressive collection of door knockers, amassed by one man over a lifetime, now going under the hammer. And Caroline is the right woman to be selling them – it turns out she’s a massive fan of door knockers too! Over at the antiques fair, which team is knocking on the door of a profit? Is it partners Rob and Sam, or married couple Janet and Bob? Expert Philip Serrell wonders whether his blues will sail away with a nautical themed jug, and Charles winds up his reds with a bird in a cage automaton – until they see the price tag. It ain’t ‘cheep’!

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A former British nurse hopes to survive tough police training to fulfil her dream of becoming a qualified constable, and an officer finally finds love.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Australia
programme.desc: Leaving Moree, Rick travels through the traditional lands of the Gomeroi people, where he meets First Nations’ pioneer Kerrie Saunders.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sonali Shah is in the Peak District helping Andrew, and his faithful dog Edna, swap Amsterdam for a home in the UK’s first National Park. Supported by his big sister, and with a budget of £375,000, he’s hoping for a characterful cottage with spectacular scenery. Property picks include homes boasting fantastic views and a Mystery House which comes with something special that should appeal to his sibling! Whilst there, Sonali also discovers how local woodlands are being transformed, as young native trees are creating a greener future following the impact of ash dieback.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: In Scotland, Izzie and Robin help Anne declutter her crammed flat to raise funds for a campervan adventure. But can a dishevelled Hindu deity bring them the fortunes they need?

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Gyles Brandreth. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: An intimate portrait of Northern Irish dancer Melissa Hamilton, charting her late start, fierce determination and rise to principal with the Royal Ballet against all expectations.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Jack struggles to cope with his emotions, Lauren prepares to make a decision, and Joel struggles being back in Walford.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 2, and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young put the 11 remaining sewers through their paces with three challenges themed around prints and colours. First, the sewers take on the Pattern Challenge, constructing a pattern-matched shell top with adaptive elements, including invisible side-zips and a high-low hem. In the Transformation Challenge, they are given second-hand clothes in purple and brown, the judges’ least-favourite colours, and have to create garments that will convince them to change their minds. Finally, in the Made to Measure, the sewers must create an eye-catching outfit in just one colour.

programme.title: Murder 24/7
programme.desc: When Jo is found stabbed at home, her husband is arrested. As forensic evidence and witness accounts are examined, detectives grow highly sceptical of his story.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's a milestone moment for the park's young Amur tigers as sisters Ginger Biscuit and Seeka begin preparations to leave home. As part of the international breeding programme, they'll soon move to new collections to help secure the future of one of the world's rarest big cats. But before they can go, the keepers face the challenge of preparing them for life apart and training them to enter their transport crates for the very first time. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at an extraordinary conservation adventure when Longleat keepers travelled to Tanzania to help renowned conservationist Tony Fitzjohn relocate endangered African wild dogs. This remarkable story would go on to influence conservation work back at the park for years to come. Elsewhere, Megan introduces the park's emus to an unusual new treat, while the recently arrived maned wolves begin settling into their new home as keepers learn to tell the three sisters apart.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: Two men are lured to a spot in Cambridgeshire under the pretence of a business meeting. But they’re kidnapped, threatened with weapons by masked men and forced to transfer a large amount of the company’s money. Police need to unpick a complicated web of phone calls and CCTV to find their moment of proof. And a couple who become ill after eating curry are found to have been poisoned. With one person dead, police are hunting for a murderer.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A fibre analyst uses a groundbreaking technique to solve the murder of 91-year-old Edwin Hiles, and a forensic fire investigator helps to uncover the truth behind a tragic house fire.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: An uncle is on hand to help his niece create a family home in Bristol. Dion’s in the dark in Leeds, but it’s nothing a lick of white paint won’t sort out. Jacqui’s in west London, where she’s hoping to get a free massage from the new owner of a ground floor flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Knock knock! Who’s there? It’s Danny Sebastian banging on about the history of door knockers, from Ancient Greece right through to the lion on the famous front door of 10 Downing Street. In Caroline Hawley’s saleroom, Danny sees an impressive collection of door knockers, amassed by one man over a lifetime, now going under the hammer. And Caroline is the right woman to be selling them – it turns out she’s a massive fan of door knockers too! Over at the antiques fair, which team is knocking on the door of a profit? Is it partners Rob and Sam, or married couple Janet and Bob? Expert Philip Serrell wonders whether his blues will sail away with a nautical themed jug, and Charles winds up his reds with a bird in a cage automaton – until they see the price tag. It ain’t ‘cheep’!

programme.title: The Moment of Proof

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Knock knock! Who’s there? It’s Danny Sebastian banging on about the history of door knockers, from Ancient Greece right through to the lion on the famous front door of 10 Downing Street. In Caroline Hawley’s saleroom, Danny sees an impressive collection of door knockers, amassed by one man over a lifetime, now going under the hammer. And Caroline is the right woman to be selling them – it turns out she’s a massive fan of door knockers too! Over at the antiques fair, which team is knocking on the door of a profit? Is it partners Rob and Sam, or married couple Janet and Bob? Expert Philip Serrell wonders whether his blues will sail away with a nautical themed jug, and Charles winds up his reds with a bird in a cage automaton – until they see the price tag. It ain’t ‘cheep’!

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sonali Shah is in the Peak District helping Andrew, and his faithful dog Edna, swap Amsterdam for a home in the UK’s first National Park. Supported by his big sister, and with a budget of £375,000, he’s hoping for a characterful cottage with spectacular scenery. Property picks include homes boasting fantastic views and a Mystery House which comes with something special that should appeal to his sibling! Whilst there, Sonali also discovers how local woodlands are being transformed, as young native trees are creating a greener future following the impact of ash dieback.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: For Rebecca Morgan-Brennan, a wig fitting is never just about choosing hair. She gives people time, privacy and clear advice as they work out what feels right for them. Some are anxious. Some are grieving the person they used to be. Others just want to feel like themselves again. This film follows Rebecca and her clients through cancer, alopecia and the moment a wig changes everything.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 2, and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young put the 11 remaining sewers through their paces with three challenges themed around prints and colours. First, the sewers take on the Pattern Challenge, constructing a pattern-matched shell top with adaptive elements, including invisible side-zips and a high-low hem. In the Transformation Challenge, they are given second-hand clothes in purple and brown, the judges’ least-favourite colours, and have to create garments that will convince them to change their minds. Finally, in the Made to Measure, the sewers must create an eye-catching outfit in just one colour.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's a milestone moment for the park's young Amur tigers as sisters Ginger Biscuit and Seeka begin preparations to leave home. As part of the international breeding programme, they'll soon move to new collections to help secure the future of one of the world's rarest big cats. But before they can go, the keepers face the challenge of preparing them for life apart and training them to enter their transport crates for the very first time. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at an extraordinary conservation adventure when Longleat keepers travelled to Tanzania to help renowned conservationist Tony Fitzjohn relocate endangered African wild dogs. This remarkable story would go on to influence conservation work back at the park for years to come. Elsewhere, Megan introduces the park's emus to an unusual new treat, while the recently arrived maned wolves begin settling into their new home as keepers learn to tell the three sisters apart.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: Two men are lured to a spot in Cambridgeshire under the pretence of a business meeting. But they’re kidnapped, threatened with weapons by masked men and forced to transfer a large amount of the company’s money. Police need to unpick a complicated web of phone calls and CCTV to find their moment of proof. And a couple who become ill after eating curry are found to have been poisoned. With one person dead, police are hunting for a murderer.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A fibre analyst uses a groundbreaking technique to solve the murder of 91-year-old Edwin Hiles, and a forensic fire investigator helps to uncover the truth behind a tragic house fire.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: An uncle is on hand to help his niece create a family home in Bristol. Dion’s in the dark in Leeds, but it’s nothing a lick of white paint won’t sort out. Jacqui’s in west London, where she’s hoping to get a free massage from the new owner of a ground floor flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Knock knock! Who’s there? It’s Danny Sebastian banging on about the history of door knockers, from Ancient Greece right through to the lion on the famous front door of 10 Downing Street. In Caroline Hawley’s saleroom, Danny sees an impressive collection of door knockers, amassed by one man over a lifetime, now going under the hammer. And Caroline is the right woman to be selling them – it turns out she’s a massive fan of door knockers too! Over at the antiques fair, which team is knocking on the door of a profit? Is it partners Rob and Sam, or married couple Janet and Bob? Expert Philip Serrell wonders whether his blues will sail away with a nautical themed jug, and Charles winds up his reds with a bird in a cage automaton – until they see the price tag. It ain’t ‘cheep’!

programme.title: Animal Park

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: Two men are lured to a spot in Cambridgeshire under the pretence of a business meeting. But they’re kidnapped, threatened with weapons by masked men and forced to transfer a large amount of the company’s money. With one person dead, police are hunting for a murderer.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A fibre analyst uses a groundbreaking technique to solve the murder of 91-year-old Edwin Hiles, and a forensic fire investigator helps to uncover the truth behind a tragic house fire.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: An uncle is on hand to help his niece create a family home in Bristol. Dion’s in the dark in Leeds, but it’s nothing a lick of white paint won’t sort out. Jacqui’s in west London, where she’s hoping to get a free massage from the new owner of a ground floor flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Knock knock! Who’s there? It’s Danny Sebastian banging on about the history of door knockers, from Ancient Greece right through to the lion on the famous front door of 10 Downing Street. In Caroline Hawley’s saleroom, Danny sees an impressive collection of door knockers, amassed by one man over a lifetime, now going under the hammer. And Caroline is the right woman to be selling them – it turns out she’s a massive fan of door knockers too! Over at the antiques fair, which team is knocking on the door of a profit? Is it partners Rob and Sam, or married couple Janet and Bob? programme.title: The Bidding Room

Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.desc: Two men are lured to a spot in Cambridgeshire under the pretence of a business meeting. But they’re kidnapped, threatened with weapons by masked men and forced to transfer a large amount of the company’s money. Police need to unpick a complicated web of phone calls and CCTV to find their moment of proof. And a couple who become ill after eating curry are found to have been poisoned. With one person dead, police are hunting for a murderer.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A fibre analyst uses a groundbreaking technique to solve the murder of 91-year-old Edwin Hiles, and a forensic fire investigator helps to uncover the truth behind a tragic house fire.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: An uncle is on hand to help his niece create a family home in Bristol. Dion’s in the dark in Leeds, but it’s nothing a lick of white paint won’t sort out. Jacqui’s in west London, where she’s hoping to get a free massage from the new owner of a ground floor flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Knock knock! Who’s there? It’s Danny Sebastian banging on about the history of door knockers, from Ancient Greece right through to the lion on the famous front door of 10 Downing Street. In Caroline Hawley’s saleroom, Danny sees an impressive collection of door knockers, amassed by one man over a lifetime, now going under the hammer. And Caroline is the right woman to be selling them – it turns out she’s a massive fan of door knockers too! Over at the antiques fair, which team is knocking on the door of a profit? Is it partners Rob and Sam, or married couple Janet and Bob? Expert Philip Serrell wonders whether his blues will sail away with a nautical themed jug, and Charles winds up his reds with a bird in a cage automaton – until they see the price tag. It ain’t ‘cheep’!

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A former British nurse hopes to survive tough police training to fulfil her dream of becoming a qualified constable, and an officer finally finds love.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Australia
programme.desc: Leaving Moree, Rick travels through the traditional lands of the Gomeroi people, where he meets First Nations’ pioneer Kerrie Saunders.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sonali Shah is in the Peak District helping Andrew, and his faithful dog Edna, swap Amsterdam for a home in the UK’s first National Park. Supported by his big sister, and with a budget of £375,000, he’s hoping for a characterful cottage with spectacular scenery. Property picks include homes boasting fantastic views and a Mystery House which comes with something special that should appeal to his sibling! Whilst there, Sonali also discovers how local woodlands are being transformed, as young native trees are creating a greener future following the impact of ash dieback.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: In Scotland, Izzie and Robin help Anne declutter her crammed flat to raise funds for a campervan adventure. But can a dishevelled Hindu deity bring them the fortunes they need?

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Gyles Brandreth. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: EastEnders

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 2, and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young put the 11 remaining sewers through their paces with three challenges themed around prints and colours. First, the sewers take on the Pattern Challenge, constructing a pattern-matched shell top with adaptive elements, including invisible side-zips and a high-low hem. In the Transformation Challenge, they are given second-hand clothes in purple and brown, the judges’ least-favourite colours, and have to create garments that will convince them to change their minds. Finally, in the Made to Measure, the sewers must create an eye-catching outfit in just one colour.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: My Kind of Town
programme.desc: Ian and Major head to the once-popular seaside resort of Girvan in Ayrshire. Ian has many happy memories of going there as a child and wants to find out how much it has changed. From the more traditional fun of the boating lake and the games arcade to newer aspects of the town like accessible bicycles and bubble football, there is something for everyone.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: On Papa Westray, Paul's visiting nephews are roped into farm work, while Paul and Mel have lots to do for their long-awaited wedding day. Their ten-year-old son and best man, Jakey, has to prepare a speech. It’s a concerning time for Sally, as some of her ewes are struck down by a devastating mystery illness. She has better luck with her stall at the Latheron Show. In Fife, Andy and Jo increase their loan to install another holiday pod and take 400 lambs to market to raise more cash.

programme.title: The Man in the Mask: An Orkney Murder
programme.desc: Bangladeshi waiter Shamsuddin Mahmood is shot dead in a shocking killing in the Orkney Isles, the first murder there for a generation. Fifteen-year-old schoolboy Michael Ross becomes the police’s prime suspect. Journalist Hazel Martin begins her investigation into a case that is full of twists and turns.

programme.title: The Man in the Mask: An Orkney Murder
programme.desc: Hazel investigates the character of convicted murderer Michael Ross. Would he have been capable as a 15-year-old schoolboy of such a brutal and cold-blooded act? She explores the background of victim Shamsuddin Mahmood and uncovers a story of two hitmen who used to live near him before he came to Orkney. Could they have been the ones who committed the murder?

programme.title: The Man in the Mask: An Orkney Murder
programme.desc: Twelve years after the murder, an eyewitness dramatically comes forward saying he saw a balaclava-clad Michael Ross with a gun near the restaurant just before the murder. Hazel investigates his story to see if it holds up. She then tests Michael Ross’s alibi and hears a new revelation about the case.

programme.title: Ray Bradshaw’s Bald Ginger
programme.desc: In his brand new stand-up special, multi-award-winning Scottish comic Ray Bradshaw talks about the problems you face when you’re a bald ginger. Filmed in front of a sold-out audience at the world-renowned Stand Comedy Club in Glasgow, Bradshaw tells of travelling the world and meeting his 'doppelgingers' (lookalikes) everywhere he goes. From sheep-shearing sheds in New Zealand to an Irish bar in Mumbai, via a Midwestern American bachelor party, Ray tells laugh-out-loud stories of the bizarre situations he gets into while trying to find as many people who look like him.

programme.title: Small Town, Big Riot
programme.desc: Mobeen Azhar investigates how a protest outside an asylum seeker hotel turned into a riot, uncovering a blueprint for a national wave of violence that eight months later would affect us all.

programme.title: Small Town, Big Riot
programme.desc: Mobeen Azhar returns to Kirkby to try to connect the dots between a whirlwind of misinformation and growing unrest outside sites housing asylum seekers. He soon finds out that a local man with white supremacist views and connections was campaigning outside the Suites hotel in the run-up to the riot. The question is, how much did this influence what took place days later? With that man now serving time in prison for stirring up racial hatred, Mobeen’s investigation takes him further afield to a former RAF base called Scampton. Since the night of the riot in Kirkby, the policy of the then Conservative government shifted. They began shutting down asylum seeker hotels in favour of bigger sites like Scampton.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: Shapeshifting Zygons are everywhere in the UK, and there is no way of knowing who to trust. With UNIT neutralised, only the Doctor stands in their way. But how do you stop a war? And what can the Doctor do to save his friends?

programme.desc: In Northern Ireland’s County Down, Jules Hudson helps Siobhan, with support from her sister, search for the perfect Emerald Isle home for her and her husband after years of living in the West Midlands. With golf firmly on the agenda, properties include a stunning house on the shores of the iconic Strangford Lough. Jules also meets a barrister turned farmer and his wife, who swapped courtrooms for country life.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: After losing both parents, a pro-footballer’s daughter calls in JB and JJ to help turn heirlooms into cash for Una’s goal - a dream holiday with her beloved pooch, Patricia.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The Great British Sewing Bee returns with brand new host Sophie Willan. Over ten weeks, 12 of the country’s best home sewers compete to be crowned winner of the Sewing Bee crown. In the opening week, judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young set three challenges on the theme of the British summer. First up, the Pattern Challenge sees them crafting summer shorts with a patch pocket. Next, in the 90-minute Transformation Challenge, barbecue aprons become bags. Finally, there is a Sewing Bee first in the Made-to-Measure challenge as the sewers are asked to create garments to fit themselves. They become their own models as they make outfits for their ideal summer’s day, and once complete, the catwalk is all theirs. One sewer will impress and earn Garment of the Week, but for another, it’s the end of the road as they leave the sewing room for good.

programme.title: BBC News

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Kemah Bob, JJ Chalmers, Kevin Clifton and Victoria Derbyshire take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp hosts this quiz show with sidekick Sarah Greene where contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: In this episode, the Beechgrove team marry sustainability with staying on-trend. Carole, Kirsty and Mairi are introduced to the plant craft of Kokedama by local house plant expert Fiona Macdonald. At her Edinburgh allotment, Kirsty demonstrates that you can still be on-trend and sustainable even if you are short of space, as she shows how to create a living-herb wall made from recycled materials.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: A camping trip with Preston goes very wrong when he won’t let them use Mojo’s tops. But camping Preston’s way soon starts a fire. It’s Mojo and Bo to the rescue!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: It's a scorcher of a day. Luckily, Duggee has a big paddling pool. Yippee! First of all, they need help with blowing up the pool and filling it with water. Thank goodness for Ethel the elephant, she can do everything. Time for the Squirrels to have lots of fun. Watch Tag, Betty, Norrie, Happy and Roly and all their animal friends have fun in the pool under the watchful eye of lifeguard Duggee.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Wow, Duggee is clever - he shows the Squirrels how to make a paper boat out of the sheets of his newspaper. And look, it floats! As they all look on in admiration, an army of ants interrupt. They need help to get across to the other side of the pond so they can join a picnic. Happy comes up with a very good idea - to make the ants a big paper boat. Duggee and the Squirrels make the ants a huge paper boat and waft them over to the other side of the pond. Tiny ant-sized hotdogs are their prize.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Mum race to escape an angry shopkeeper in their game of driving.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: At school, Bluey and her friends turn a tree stump into a thrilling helicopter game. But as the pilot, Bluey has to learn to give up some control so they can all have fun.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Grandmaster Glitch tries his hand at stunt flying, but the Grimbots are unimpressed, giving him a unanimous thumbs down. He tries again, but it's one loop-the-loop too much for poor old Grim HQ and it crash-lands in the branches of a baobab tree. Lars makes friends with a baby lemur whose family has been scared away by a bright light and loud banging in the distance. The team investigates and discovers the cause: Grandmaster Glitch is illuminating Grim HQ with floodlights, while his Grimbots try to dislodge it from the tree.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Cheeky Peter Rabbit loves adventure but he struggles to stay out of trouble. Luckily his best friends are always around to help him out. Based on Beatrix Potter's classic stories.

programme.title: Octonauts

programme.title: Numberblocks

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. Sing along as Magic E makes mischief and shows you how to turn a cap into a cape.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: When a jukebox washes up, its catchy song proves a hit among the Piripenguins, driving Pancake up the wall. A solution is needed, but how can he stop a seemingly unstoppable trend?

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Zog and the doctors want to find Fergus a friend to cure his loneliness. Boom, Twiggy and Mara all try to be his new pal.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Bryan gets spooked and thinks there’s a lake monster lurking in the mists. It’ll be Mojo and Bo who have to find the monster... or show Bryan that there’s no monster at all!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing's friends are coming to his house for a cake party. Sula arrives first and Bing can't wait to show her the cake he has made, but he accidentally tips the cake off its stand and breaks it into pieces. Bing is upset that the cake is ruined but Amma helps him see it somewhat differently.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘crab’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. Today, we see different crabs that can walk sideways, hide, have big claws or are colourful. Dee makes friends with a crab by the seaside and even meets a king crab. The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie, Triggs and Dad are making a special cake for Granny. Dad is extremely careful about following the recipe, but Maddie has a slightly looser approach. Okay, a lot looser… Will their new bonkers cake pass the Granny test?

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: The Piggies are called to find Fred’s lost book, but his bookshelf collapses when they arrive! The Piggies split up: Charlie and Cornelia repair the shelf, while Cesar searches with neighbours... who end up giving them even more books to organise!

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos watch an artist make his clay sculpture's head smaller. The Twirlywoos then have a go and make the whole sculpture smaller and smaller until it is smaller than the Twirlywoos! The Twirlywoos are visited by the Piece of Paper. The Piece of Paper folds itself up smaller and smaller and smaller still! Peekaboo comes out of his hole to see what is going on and the Piece of Paper unfolds itself so that it covers Peekaboo!

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin visits a friend’s school to make a recycled dragon and to take part in a dragon parade. Meanwhile, it’s school photo day with Teacher Tumble - say cheese!

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Preschool series. The Teletubbies have fun bumping into one another and watch children in Tummy Tales play in bumper cars.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Felicity, Idris, Zadie, Tommy, Remi, George and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are bath toys which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate bath toys inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The popular nursery rhyme ‘Row, Row, Row Your Boat’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children create rainbow art, learn British Sign Language signs for red, rainbow and pink, then sing and sign the colourful song, I Can Sing a Rainbow.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Aaron, Isla and Novah go digging with Chatterpot to explore wiggly roots and find out how they help plants grow tall. They also discover that some are tasty too!

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: The baby zebras learn that exercise can be lots of fun. Hamza visits the watering hole – a place where lots of wild animals gather. He also joins the elephants on a forest walk.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri and Lou scare each other with bedtime stories.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: A game of 'grannies' is fun, until Bluey and Bingo can't agree on one simple question: Can Grannies dance? Now they need to video call Nana to get the answer.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Norrie is upset when she sees a leaf fall from the tree. She thinks it's broken. She soon cheers up when she finds out that some trees shed their leaves in autumn, and actually it's quite good fun playing and jumping in piles of leaves. But ouch! What has Roly found stuck to his bottom? It's an acorn. Duggee explains that lots of forest animals collect acorns to eat in the winter, so the Squirrels decide to look and find lots of acorns to share out for everyone.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: It's lunchtime in Colourland! Red invites her friends for lunch, where they try each other’s favourite foods.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Gabi and Izzy want to find out all about sea anemones in today’s episode. Rory and Sandy head to the beach to look for them, whilst Chantelle meets a sea anemone expert on a night-time rockpool safari. In the Teeny Tiny Task, Rory and Sandy play a game of catch, as they pretend to be sea anemones trying to catch their food, with colourful balls and a bucket. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files help explain all of Gabi and Izzy’s questions. With the help of the Teeny Tiny Creatures poem, we discover that, like lots of other teeny tiny creatures, sea anemones are superheroes and help our planet in their own special way.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Henry and his little sister Sophie make crowns and become King Henry and Queen Sophie. Along with their noble knights (Mummy and Mama!), they head to the local park on a royal quest to rescue their toy turtle Pebbles, who is trapped in a castle! Back home, the royals relax with a rainbow waterfall and water squirters. It’s not long before Henry and the whole family are soaking wet!

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Children’s cookery series with Big Cook Jen and Little Cook Small. Jen is pretending to be Jiggly Cook, the jelly juggler. Small is worried that jelly is going to be hard to juggle. Small finds out where potatoes grow, and they make snow family pie for today’s customer, Sid the Snowman.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Kika is a golden labrador and a guide dog for her owner Dr Amit, who is blind, which means he cannot see. She is trained to use her super sight to help Dr Amit do as many things as he can by himself. Together, they make the best team! Dr Amit is off to the florist's to buy some flowers for his wife, Seema. To help him get there, Kika enlists the help of top secret 'bumpy bits', the system of clever dots and lines on the pavement that humans call tactile paving. As they navigate their way over a zebra crossing, along a footpath next to a cycle lane, down a stairway near the station and across the road at a pelican crossing, with its top secret spinning cone, Kika explains how the different bumpy bits help her and Dr Amit find their way around town. It’s like reading a secret code. Dr Amit wears shoes that he can feel the different bumps through. And when he finds shoes that are good for the bumps, he buys five pairs! But on their way back from the florist's, Kika finds their path blocked. Can she use her super sight find a new way home in time to give Seema her flowers?

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: It’s Miss Gerrard’s birthday, and the children plan a surprise party for her. Felicity and Coen are the chefs. They are in charge of baking and decorating a delicious birthday cake, with help from Mrs Bailey. Theo and Jasper are making a beautiful birthday crown for Miss Gerrard to wear and have asked Mrs Hussain to help them. With everything ready, it’s time for the surprise party!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle learns that the summer holidays will soon be over and Evie will be going to school. Determined not to be left alone, Waffle hatches a plan to keep the family at home.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona and Isabelle are going fishing, so Bernie volunteers to mind Baba and Lala. The little pufflings are having a great time playing with their ball, and Bernie settles down to watch. When the ball falls into the burrows, Baba and Lala lead Bernie on an underground adventure to find it. There's still life in the old shell yet!

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: It’s been raining, and Toad is resisting the urge to join in with Yukee and her friends' game of musical mud-squelching. However, he can’t resist the muddy beat and is soon squelching with his friends.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs are helping Mum babysit their little neighbour Sally. She's a toddler and is just learning to speak. Maddie really wants Sally to enjoy herself, but no matter what she offers, Sally just keeps saying 'no'! Could it be that this trickster toddler is saying 'no' even when she means something else?

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Kitty wants a racetrack. For Cornelia, it's the perfect opportunity to prove she's the fastest builder... but she works too quickly and doesn't manage to get it right. Fortunately, the Piggy Builders know how to work as a team to give themselves a second chance.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: A fantastic treat awaits the Numberblocks if they can figure out how to ride the rays to the top of Ray Canyon. Solve a number puzzle with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Something Special

Upset, Love Monster runs away and asks Elder Kitten for his help. Elder Kitten realises Love Monster's mistake and explains that he isn't an elder yet - but that he's done a very elder-y thing in asking for help.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A group of ten strangers arrive at Danny and Emily's manor to compete for up to £100,000 in a brand-new game where survival depends not only on how smart you are, but how smart others think you are... From the moment they arrive, the players are thrown straight into brain-teasing challenges, keeping them occupied outside the gate. The first private pod quiz introduces the show's central tension: money is earned in secret, then publicly declared. Exaggeration, denial and bluffing creep in fast, leaving the group unsure who to trust. When the house must decide who they believe has contributed the least to the prize pot, personal grudges and first impressions start to outweigh evidence - but with half the prize pot at stake for ejecting the wrong player, the stakes couldn't be higher.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A group of ten strangers arrive at Danny and Emily's manor to compete for up to £100,000 in a brand-new game where survival depends not only on how smart you are, but how smart others think you are... From the moment they arrive, the players are thrown straight into brain-teasing challenges, keeping them occupied outside the gate. The first private pod quiz introduces the show's central tension: money is earned in secret, then publicly declared. Exaggeration, denial and bluffing creep in fast, leaving the group unsure who to trust. When the house must decide who they believe has contributed the least to the prize pot, personal grudges and first impressions start to outweigh evidence - but with half the prize pot at stake for ejecting the wrong player, the stakes couldn't be higher.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A group of ten strangers arrive at Danny and Emily's manor to compete for up to £100,000 in a brand-new game where survival depends not only on how smart you are, but how smart others think you are... From the moment they arrive, the players are thrown straight into brain-teasing challenges, keeping them occupied outside the gate. The first private pod quiz introduces the show's central tension: money is earned in secret, then publicly declared. Exaggeration, denial and bluffing creep in fast, leaving the group unsure who to trust. When the house must decide who they believe has contributed the least to the prize pot, personal grudges and first impressions start to outweigh evidence - but with half the prize pot at stake for ejecting the wrong player, the stakes couldn't be higher.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A group of ten strangers arrive at Danny and Emily's manor to compete for up to £100,000 in a brand-new game where survival depends not only on how smart you are, but how smart others think you are... From the moment they arrive, the players are thrown straight into brain-teasing challenges, keeping them occupied outside the gate. The first private pod quiz introduces the show's central tension: money is earned in secret, then publicly declared. Exaggeration, denial and bluffing creep in fast, leaving the group unsure who to trust. When the house must decide who they believe has contributed the least to the prize pot, personal grudges and first impressions start to outweigh evidence - but with half the prize pot at stake for ejecting the wrong player, the stakes couldn't be higher.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A group of ten strangers arrive at Danny and Emily's manor to compete for up to £100,000 in a brand-new game where survival depends not only on how smart you are, but how smart others think you are... From the moment they arrive, the players are thrown straight into brain-teasing challenges, keeping them occupied outside the gate. The first private pod quiz introduces the show's central tension: money is earned in secret, then publicly declared. Exaggeration, denial and bluffing creep in fast, leaving the group unsure who to trust. When the house must decide who they believe has contributed the least to the prize pot, personal grudges and first impressions start to outweigh evidence - but with half the prize pot at stake for ejecting the wrong player, the stakes couldn't be higher.
